Main's US market beta is 0.55 versus 0.61 for the benchmark, although both hold 60% equity: the international sleeve moves less than one-for-one with the US market (VEA 0.77, VWO 0.61). The active market beta is -0.054 (t -11.5).

The active return also loads on size (SMB +0.063, t +11.0), value (HML +0.030, t +3.6) and, negatively, on profitability (RMW -0.031, t -4.3). These factors explain 37% of daily active-return variation; the rest is likely non-US equity and currency exposure, which US factors do not span.

Average active return was -1.48% a year (arithmetic). The lower market beta cost -0.58% in a strong US market, the small-cap tilt -0.27% and profitability -0.16%, while value added +0.22%. The remaining alpha of -0.67% has t = -0.9: factor tilts account for about 55% of the shortfall, and the rest cannot be distinguished from noise.

US equity factors describe the bond ETFs poorly (R2 BND 0.09, IEF 0.06, BNDX 0.06) and the international equity ETFs only partly (VEA 0.70, VWO 0.48). Portfolio-level alphas therefore absorb unmodelled bond and foreign returns and are not interpreted; the active-return regression, where bonds largely cancel, is the informative one.
Adding RMW, CMA and momentum to the three-factor model raises the active-return R2 only from 0.35 to 0.37; size and market explain most of what the US factors can explain.
